To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

MDM2 SNP 309 G allele was significantly associated favorable outcome in female patients with gliobastomas, and the TP53 codon72 Pro allele was a significant risk factor in patients with TP53 mutation and those treated with surgery and radiotherapy.

(i) MDM2 SNP 309 is associated with favorable prognosis in female gliobastoma patients; (ii) TP53 codon72 polymorphism is associated with age at onset and survival of glioblastoma; and (iii) TP53 mutation and TP53 codons 72 polymorphism are associated with age at diagnosis and survival in glioblastoma.
MDM2 polymorphism SNP309 is associated both with favorable survival in female gliobastoma patients and with the presence of the TP53 codon72 Pro/Pro polymorphism.

the MDM2 gene SNP309 and TP53 gene codon 72, which are two of the most studied polymorphisms in the p53 pathway.

MDM2 polymorphism SNP309 is not a risk factor for glioblastoma.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MDM2 T309G polymorphism is not associated with survival in glioblastoma.
MDM2 and p53 polymorphisms are related to the clinical features and outcomes of glioblastomas patients.
TP53 codons 72 and 248 polymorphisms, and the MDM2 polymorphism SNP309, are significantly associated with patient age and prognosis of glioblastomas and may have important clinical implications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MDM2 309G allele may be a favorable prognostic factor in female gliobastomas, while the TP53 Pro72 allele may be a negative prognostic factor, especially for patients with TP53 mutations or those treated with surgery and radiotherapy.

MDM2 SNPs and TP53 codons 72 and 248 polymorphisms may be useful in identifying subgroups of glioblastoma that have distinct biological characteristics, and may benefit from different therapeutic approaches.
MDM2 and/or TP53 polymorphisms can influence the outcome of patients with gliobastoma.
